why: The review gate's trigger filter is the one piece of this repository's security machinery whose failure mode is silence: a filter that misses a path produces no red check, no annotation and no log line — just a PR page where the security gate is absent. Fifteen mutants, in three groups. Five break the filter itself (the regression, replayed). Six break the matcher or the workflow reader, because a coverage test built on a matcher that says yes to everything is a green light wired to nothing. Four break the derivation, since a surface that quietly stops finding files reports full coverage of an empty set.

mutants.why: The narrowest plausible version of the original defect: someone widens the filter for the package they are working on and leaves the webhook and controller out.
One `*` instead of two stops at the first directory boundary, so `config/rbac/role.yaml` falls out while the glob still looks right.
`examples/` holds NetworkPolicies and RBAC overlays that people apply verbatim; it looks like documentation and is not.

edits.find: "examples/**" # NetworkPolicies and RBAC overlays people apply verbatim

mutants.why: `cmd/broker/main.go` is where the broker's TLS is configured; a filter that covers the package but not the entrypoint misses the wiring.
If the workflow no longer triggers on itself, the one change that can disable the gate is the one change the gate never sees.
Reading `**/agents/**` as requiring at least one leading directory is the plausible misreading, and it would silently exempt every path at the repository root.
Treating `*` as `.*` makes every narrow glob quietly broad, so a filter that does not cover the surface reports that it does.
The purest vacuous pass: coverage is total because nothing is ever unmatched.

edits.find: return any(github_glob_to_regex(p).match(path) for p in patterns)
edits.replace: return True if patterns else False

mutants.why: The opposite failure, included because a matcher can also break in the direction that makes the check unfixably red and invites someone to delete it.

edits.find: return any(github_glob_to_regex(p).match(path) for p in patterns)
edits.replace: return False and bool(patterns and path)

mutants.why: The added globs sit below a comment line. A reader that treats a comment as the end of the list sees only the nine original patterns and never says so.

edits.find: continue  # interleaved comments are the norm in this block
edits.replace: break  # interleaved comments are the norm in this block

mutants.why: One hyphen inverts the entire filter: the gate would run on everything EXCEPT the security surface. A reader that fetches a list by shape rather than by name would report the same nine globs and pass.
Without `synchronize` the gate reviews the opening commit and nothing after it, so a PR can go green and then grow the change that needed reviewing.
Lose the TLS and token-review arm and the broker's authenticator stops being security surface — coverage then passes over a set that no longer contains the file the whole finding was about.
A typo in the kind regex empties the largest source silently; 41 of the 65 derived files vanish and the coverage assertion still reports zero uncovered.

If the enumeration itself yields nothing, every derived set is empty and every assertion about them is trivially satisfied — the LSN-021 shape, a check running green over nothing at all. The neighbouring failure, a bare `git ls-files` that sees the index and not the working tree (LSN-050), is deliberately NOT a mutant here: it cannot be caught by this suite, because at the moment the suite runs in CI everything is committed. `invariants-gate.py` carries that one, and it caught this very file on its first run.

edits.replace: return [f for f in repo_files(REPO) if f.startswith("nothing/")]
